paras: The lynching of a cowboy near Downing's sawmill was the killing of an unnamed man in Cochise County, Arizona Territory, some time in early 1882. He was said to have confessed to stealing mules and work oxen from the mill, and the case is known only from a brief correspondent's letter that mentioned it among complaints about stock theft.

Writing to the San Francisco Bulletin, a correspondent in a camp in what the letter printed as "Cachise county" complained that "trouble and loss" were still being caused by "cow boys." About six weeks before the letter, the mules and work oxen at Major Downing's sawmill, twenty miles from the camp, had been stolen.

Since the theft, according to the correspondent, a cowboy had been lynched near the sawmill "after having confessed, it is said, that he was the thief." The letter gives no name or race for the man, no date or method, and nothing about who killed him or how many took part.
No report of an inquest, arrests or other follow-up appears in the coverage.

The Lambertville Record of New Jersey reprinted the Bulletin correspondent's paragraph on April 26, 1882, under the heading "Life in Arizona." The lynching appears there in a single sentence, set between the theft at Downing's mill and the running off of a ranchman's vaquero stock, without comment on the killing itself. The writer used the item to complain that settlers lacked protection against thieves, saying such losses would be unsurprising only under "some petty European Government" that did not pretend to protect its subjects.

bases: The only report says a cowboy 'has been lynched' near the sawmill after reportedly confessing to a theft (A1).

A1 uses the word 'lynched' for the killing of a man said to have confessed to stealing stock, which implies an extralegal killing as punishment for a crime, but it gives no detail of who killed him or how many took part.
One reprinted correspondent's paragraph (A1) is the only report found; the original San Francisco Bulletin item and any local Arizona report were not found.
